title: Gradual Shift Rehearsal Dock: lightweight UX for drafting, simulating, and rehearsing traffic shifts with rollback exercises
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design a compact, dock-style UI that sits in the Redwood Console rollout screen and lets engineers and PMs author, preview, and rehearse gradual traffic shifts (time-based ramps, tapered windows, and step changes). The dock should support: 1) visual drafting with a configurable curve editor (start/stop, ramp slope, hold windows, step points), 2) fast simulation against historical traffic profiles with latency/cost impact overlays, 3) dry-run mode that simulates production behavior and surfaces expected errors and fallback triggers, 4) one-click rollback rehearsal that shows why a rollback would trigger (metrics and assertion failures) and lets users practice an emergency rollback flow. Key goals: reduce deployment anxiety, make tradeoffs between latency and cost visible during plan time, and make rollbacks predictable and testable before live traffic changes.
acceptance_criteria: Dock can be opened from any rollout draft and persisted as a named template
Users can author at least three curve types: linear ramp, sigmoid/taper, and stepped split
Simulation shows estimated token cost delta and 95th latency impact for the selected curve based on historical traces
Dry-run mode produces a timeline with simulated assertions and a visible rollback trigger that can be replayed
Design passes accessibility review (keyboard operable, color contrast >= 4.5:1 for critical indicators)
Design files and interaction specs handed off to engineering with annotated responsive behavior
comments: 2026-02-25 Priya Kapoor: Initial brief — propose a dock to keep the authoring context near the rollout timeline. Emphasize quick rehearsal without creating full canary environments.
2026-03-01 Zoe Park: Low-fidelity mocks delivered. Chose curve editor over manual percentage table to reduce cognitive load for multi-step ramps. Noted need to show cost delta inline.

2026-03-03 Daniel Ortiz (ENG): Flagged backend needs: an endpoint to simulate token cost for a candidate curve and an aggregation job to replay historical traces for dry-runs. Suggested a dev spike (ENG-21241).
2026-03-05 Mateo Silva (PM): Requested a lightweight template library and shareable links for runbooks. Prioritized brief training microcopy and a ‘safety checklist’ in the dock.

2026-03-08 Accessibility review (Alice Nguyen): Recommended keyboard-first controls for curve editor and persistent textual summaries for colorblind users. Also noted ARIA labeling requirements for rollback rehearsal replay controls.
2026-03-10 Zoe Park: High-fidelity prototype uploaded. Microinteractions added: snap-to-keypoints, hover tooltips with cost/latency delta, and inline validation for invalid ramp shapes.

2026-03-11 Daniel Ortiz (ENG): Engineering review — agreed on API contract for simulation. Requested simplified animation for rehearsal replay to reduce CPU while still conveying sequence. Blocking note: needs ENG-22901 for trace replay infra.
2026-03-12 Priya Kapoor: Updated acceptance criteria and moved to In Review. Added test scenario doc for runbook writers and ops training.
2026-03-12 Reviewer comment (Mateo Silva): Please add an explicit ‘abort rehearsal’ CTA and clarify how dry-run differs from canary preview in copy.
decisions: Use curve-editor as primary authoring surface; fallback to table input for quick edits and accessibility
Expose cost delta and 95th latency estimate inline using a compact badge that updates live
Dry-run will be a simulated trace replay, not a traffic-mirroring feature; production mirroring remains a separate action
Rollback rehearsal will show the top 3 metric assertions that would trigger an automatic rollback and allow users to step through the automated rollback flow
Templates are saved as JSON blobs tied to project IDs and can be shared between teams via a template library
reviewer_feedback: Daniel Ortiz (ENG): Backend needs dedicated sim endpoints; prefer knobs for simulation fidelity vs cost. Keep UI animations minimal to avoid client perf issues.
Mateo Silva (PM): Love the rehearsal playback. Add a quick tour and an option to export the rehearsal as a snapshot for postmortems.
Alice Nguyen (Design Lead): Polish microcopy for failure states; ensure focus states are obvious. Consider a condensed ‘mobile drop-in’ for runway edits on smaller widths.
